text: Gold bounced about 0.4% to near $3,892 in early US trading after Thursday's 13-month low near $3,852; it is still down about 3.5% for the week.
Silver was flat near $49.96, so the gold/silver ratio rose to about 77.9; SLV and AGQ trade on silver.
October producer prices rose 0.3%, a bit less than the 0.4% expected, but the yearly rate hit 6.5%, the highest since November 2022.
The 10-year yield stayed near 5.13% and the dollar index held above 103 after the report, which keeps pressure on gold and the miners (GDX, GDXJ, GDXU).
Stock futures edged higher before the open (S&P 500 futures about +0.4%, Nasdaq 100 about +0.1%) as Nvidia rebounded in premarket trading; this matters for QQQ, TQQQ and SQQQ.
Bitcoin fell below $70,000 for the first time since August, to about $69,135 at 8:30 AM ET, after more than $1 billion in forced liquidations.
USD/JPY hovered just under 160 as Japanese officials warned about rapid currency moves.
Brent held near $96 after Thursday's jump, while the IEA said oil supply has moved ahead of demand again; this matters for NRGU.
